text: dsh-cli-bridge 是面向 DSH 网页端的编码任务委派插件。它向 DSH 注册模型工具、/cli 命令和浏览器实时面板，把任务交给 Claude Code 或 Codex CLI 执行，并将运行过程流式展示。用户可以单独或并行委派任务、查看状态与输出、回答问题或继续已有任务，也能管理账户和 CLI 工具链；并行任务使用独立 Git worktree。自动决策、继续和审查可按配置启用。适合希望在 DSH 对话中调用本地编码代理并跟踪工作的开发者；需要 Node.js 24 以上，以及 Claude Code 或 Codex 的登录账户或凭据。

dsh-cli-bridge lets DSH web delegate coding tasks to Claude Code or Codex CLI and stream activity to a live panel. Tools and /cli support single or parallel tasks, replies, account and CLI management, and Git worktrees. Requires Node.js 24 or later and a CLI account or credentials.
想让 DSH 把一个编码任务交给 Claude Code 或 Codex 处理。
我想在网页里实时看到编码代理运行时做了什么。
能不能同时派发几个互不依赖的开发任务，各自在独立分支完成？
让 DSH 帮我管理 Claude Code 和 Codex 的账户与安装。
I want to continue a coding task by answering the agent's question without starting over.
Can I watch delegated coding work live in my DSH web interface?
dsh-cli-bridge 的功能「委派编码任务」：通过模型工具把任务交给 Claude Code 或 Codex CLI，并等待运行结果。可指定代理、账户、模型和 effort。
dsh-cli-bridge 的功能「实时运行面板」：任务运行时，网页端接收流式输出、活动和状态更新，用户可在界面跟踪进度。
dsh-cli-bridge 的功能「并行任务」：使用批量委派工具提交多个独立任务，每项获得自己的 Git worktree，完成后逐项处理合并。
dsh-cli-bridge 的功能「续接任务」：使用回复工具回答代理提出的问题或发送后续指令，继续原有委派会话。
dsh-cli-bridge 的功能「账户与工具链管理」：在启用管理工具时，查看和管理 CLI 账户，并查看、安装或更新代理 CLI。
dsh-cli-bridge 使用前须知：Node.js 要求为 24 或更高版本；managed 工具链默认会尝试自动安装缺失的 CLI。
我想从 /cli 查看可用模型并手动控制正在运行的任务。
I need several independent coding jobs to run in parallel without sharing a working tree.

dsh-cli-bridge README · What it does：**One request in the chat. Claude Code or Codex doing real work — on screen, in
real time, under your control.**

`dsh-cli-bridge` hands work to **Claude Code** and **Codex**, then keeps you and
DeepSeek Harness in the loop for the whole job:

dsh-cli-bridge README · What it does：| **📺 Watch it live**                                                                                                      | **🧠 Give DSH the wheel**                                                                                                         | **🛠️ Nothing to set up**                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Every command, every file changed, every line of thought appears in DSH as it happens — not a spinner, not a final paste. | DeepSeek can steer, answer, and review the work on its own, step after step — or hand you the question when it should not decide. | It handles Claude Code and Codex for you. You install one plugin; it takes care of the rest. |

dsh-cli-bridge README · What it does：> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Why this exists** — the built-in Claude Code and Codex integration runs in
> the background and returns only the final message. You can't see what it is
> doing, and it bills you twice. `dsh-cli-bridge` shows the whole job on screen,
> keeps the details out of your conversation, and gives DeepSeek the controls.

dsh-cli-bridge README · The difference：| The built-in way                       | ✨ `dsh-cli-bridge`                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| ❌ you get only the final result       | ✅ the whole job, live in DSH                             |
| ❌ DeepSeek just reads the answer      | ✅ DeepSeek steers, answers, and reviews the work         |
| ❌ you set them up yourself            | ✅ everything is set up for you                           |
| ❌ one login, set up by hand           | ✅ many separate accounts, side by side                   |
| ❌ tasks share one folder              | ✅ each task gets its own copy, merged back automatically |
| ❌ Claude Code talks to Anthropic only | ✅ Claude Code + Codex, plus any compatible provider      |

dsh-cli-bridge README · And the rest：The headline is watching it live. The rest is what makes it safe to let Claude
Code or Codex loose on a project:

dsh-cli-bridge README · And the rest：- **👥 Multi-account, isolated** — each account is kept separate; one login
  never touches another.
- **🌐 Any provider** — Claude Code can reach DeepSeek, OpenRouter, or any
  compatible provider.
- **🌿 Its own copy & automatic merge** — several tasks each get their own copy;
  finished work is merged back automatically, one at a time, and conflicts are
  kept for you.
- **🧭 It asks clearly** — when it needs a decision, it asks you plainly instead
  of guessing.
- **🔒 Respects your settings** — it follows your Read Only / Workspace Write /
  Full Access choice, and adds no rules of its own.
- **⚙️ Model & effort per task** — each task can name its own model and how hard
  to try, or use sensible defaults.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cli-bridge
```

---

dsh-cli-bridge README · Getting started：1. **Install** the plugin once, in a terminal:

```sh
   dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cli-bridge
   ```

2. **Open** DeepSeek Harness and start a conversation.

3. **Ask**, in the message box, what you want. For example:

> "Use Claude Code to add a login page."

DeepSeek takes it from there: it walks you through signing in (a box opens in
   the browser for the code) and runs the work with Claude Code or Codex while
   you watch.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Signing in (accounts)：The first time you ask for something, DeepSeek helps you sign in to Claude Code
or Codex. A box opens in the browser — type the code and press Enter.

Each account stays separate, so you can keep more than one. Just ask:

- "Add my other Claude Code account."
- "Make that one the default."
- "Use my Claude Code API key instead of a login."

dsh-cli-bridge README · What you can ask for：- **One task** — "Use Claude Code to fix the failing tests."
- **Several tasks at once** — "Use Codex to add the login page, and Claude Code
  to write the tests." Each runs on its own copy of the project and is merged
  back when done.
- **A specific model or effort** — name a model loosely ("use opus", "use
  sonnet") or ask it to think harder. `/cli models` lists exactly what each
  delegate accepts, and anything close is understood.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Manual or automatic：By default, nothing happens without you: if Claude Code or Codex has a question,
it asks you, right in the chat.

To let it work more on its own, type `/cli auto decide on` (it answers its own
questions), `/cli auto continue on` (it keeps going through remaining work), and
`/cli auto review on` (it checks the finished work). Use `off` instead of `on`
to undo any of them.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Manual or automatic：`/cli` tells you when the switches can actually act. Auto decisions are made by
the same DeepSeek model that is running the conversation, so a switch needs a
model route — when there is none, every question still comes to you, and it says
so instead of quietly doing nothing. A task that ran under auto reports which
switches were on and which model decided.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Watching and steering：Everything runs live in the conversation — every command, every file change.
While it runs you can answer its questions, tell it what to do next, or stop it.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Where the work goes：One task runs right in your project. Several at once each run on their own copy
(a git branch) and are merged back when done. If two changes touch the same
line, nothing is lost — you are told there is a conflict to resolve.

dsh-cli-bridge README · Doing it yourself (optional)：You never need to. But typing `/cli` shows what's ready and your accounts, and
`/cli models`, `/cli login claude personal` and `/cli auto` let you drive it by
hand if you prefer.
